Explore Services About

Wild Kinematics helps researchers and organizations design movement studies, capture high-quality motion data, and turn it into meaningful biological insights.

Biology comes first: we help obtaining measurements that are most relevant to your biological question.

Why measure behavior through kinematics?

Subtle maneuvers, escape speeds, or behavioral displays often happen too fast or are too nuanced for standard video or observation. Using high-resolution kinematics allow extracting precise metrics, revealing deeper mechanisms (energy cost, inter-individual differences in behavior or performance...).

Acquiring appropriate, reliable kinematic measurements can feel like a learning a whole new discipline.

You may find yourself in one of these situations:

  • Unsure where to start with hardware: Choosing camera placements, frame rates, and lighting setups adapted to your biological question.
  • Overwhelmed by video tracking tools: Deciding whether to invest in commercial tracking platforms or use open-source algorithms.
  • Stuck with raw footage: Sitting on hundreds of gigabytes of video without a clear analytical pipeline to extract meaningful variables.

This is where Wild Kinematics can help.

About

Camille Le Roy, PhD

Researcher, Field Biologist, and Biomechanist

Hi, I'm Camille.

My background is rooted in evolutionary biology. Driven by a passion for understanding how animal movement evolves and diversifies, I specialized in combining ecology and evolution with biomechanics, with a focus on insect flight.

Fun fact: I originally wanted to become a wildlife filmmaker. I ended up as a researcher, filming animals to decode the evolution of their behavior.

To study the evolution of animal movement, I learned the nuts and bolts of quantifying motion: configuring high-speed camera setups, reconstructing 3D trajectories, and extracting biologically meaningful metrics. My research also involved a lot of fieldwork, whereby I've designed setups to capture motion in fully natural settings.

My career brought me to work closely alongside physicists and aerospace engineers. This gave me deep familiarity with biomechanical tools and engineering principles, and hence a great perspective on how to combine biological and engineering approaches.

I created Wild Kinematics to bring movement quantification within reach for more researchers, helping break down the barriers between ecology, behavior, and biomechanics.
